title: Choking — adult or child over 1 year
confirm_prompt: This sounds like choking. Can they still cough or speak? Say go, or tap Continue, and I'll talk you through it.

steps.text: First, ask them out loud: are you choking? If they can cough, speak, or breathe, do not hit them. Stay with them and tell them to keep coughing.
If they cannot cough, speak, or breathe, stand to the side and just behind them. Support their chest with one hand and lean them well forward.
Give up to five sharp blows between their shoulder blades with the heel of your other hand. Check after each one to see if the blockage has cleared.
If it has not cleared, stand behind them and put both arms around their waist. Make a fist just above their belly button and grasp it with your other hand.
Pull sharply inwards and upwards, up to five times. Check between each one.
Keep alternating: five back blows, then five thrusts. Do not stop while they are still choking.
If they stop responding at any point, lower them to the floor, call for help now, and start chest compressions if you know how.

sources: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines 2020 — Choking
International Liaison Committee on Resuscitation (ILCOR), Consensus on Science with Treatment Recommendations — Foreign Body Airway Obstruction
